description:
The single fixture inventory for contracts/auth/v1/jsonschema/principal.v1.schema.json, read by the Go, Python and TypeScript golden runners. ONE manifest, ONE fixture directory, three runners -- three copies of the same fixtures is the drift class G-70 exists to catch, so a runner that maintains its own list is a review defect.

`accept` is a positive control corpus and carries equal weight to `reject`: a validator that is too strict passes every rejection test while breaking every real caller, and that failure mode is invisible to a suite that only asserts rejections.
format_assertion_note: Two different things, do not conflate them. (1) CROSS-LANGUAGE FLOOR: every constraint a reject fixture asserts must be expressible in a keyword all three validators enforce -- in practice `pattern`, never `format`, because github.com/google/jsonschema-go records `format` and ignores it during validation (its own doc.go, "Deviations from the specification"). (2) DEFENCE IN DEPTH where available: the Python and TypeScript runners MUST still enable format assertion (Python: Draft202012Validator(format_checker=...), which needs rfc3339-validator installed or it silently registers no date-time checker; TypeScript: ajv-formats) and MUST FAIL rather than skip if they cannot -- a format check that silently checks nothing while exiting 0 is the exact defect this contract exists to prevent.

reject.why: ACP-ADR-05 decision 4 / G-27: a single-segment action is the is_admin shape, made unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.
ACP-ADR-07 decision 2 and G-14: entitlement must never travel inside a credential. This fixture is the executable form of that ADR -- re-adding tier/licensed_features to the principal turns this red.

Draft 2020-12 makes `format` annotation-only unless the validator opts in, and github.com/google/jsonschema-go ignores it outright (its doc.go, "Deviations from the specification"). The enforced keyword here is therefore `pattern`, which all three validators apply identically; the schema also carries `format: date-time`, which Python and TypeScript assert as a stricter calendar check on top. Asserting `pattern` rather than `format` is what makes this fixture mean the same thing in all three languages.

REGRESSION GUARD for a MEASURED cross-language divergence, not a hypothetical one. With the digit class spelled \d this exact document was ACCEPTED by the Python validator and REJECTED by the Go one: Python's `re` treats \d as Unicode and matches Devanagari digits, while Go RE2 and ECMA-262 treat it as ASCII. The schemas now spell every digit class [0-9], and this fixture is what stops a future edit reintroducing \d -- under \d it turns green in Python and stays red in Go, which is precisely the one-language-disagrees drift the cross-language corpus exists to catch.
impersonation is REQUIRED and explicitly nullable, so a deserializer that defaults a missing object to a zero value cannot silently read absent as not-impersonating.
ACP-ADR-03 bounds the impersonation session at 15 minutes; an impersonation object with no expiry is an unbounded delegated session.
Empty string is not null. Python treats "" as falsy where Go nil-checks a pointer, so a contract that accepted "" would mean two different things in two runtimes.
A duplicated action makes set-cardinality reasoning about the permission set wrong.
ACP-ADR-05 decision 3 / G-31: every allow-cache key binds all four revisions. A partial revisions object would let a consumer build a cache key that a bump cannot invalidate.
A relying party must reject an unrecognised contract version rather than parse optimistically.
A credential generation counter is monotonic and non-negative.
ACP-ADR-05 decision 1: unknown denies. The vocabulary is the Wave 0 closed set.

regex_dialect_note: Every `pattern` in these schemas must stay inside the common subset of Go RE2, ECMA-262 and Python `re`. RE2 has no back-references and no lookaround, so a pattern using them either errors or means something different in Go than in the other two -- silently, on the permissive side. google/jsonschema-go names this deviation explicitly. Guarded by a test, not left to review.
